p01: Create a NEW botanical educational 2x2 sprite sheet, four separate illustrations with true transparent alpha background, no text, no arrows or frames. TOP LEFT: enlarged portion of Fragaria vesca terminal leaflet EDGE, a curved obovate blade fragment with five coarse pointed teeth leaning toward apex, cream veins ending at tooth tips, blade portion only, not a whole leaf. TOP RIGHT: enlarged portion of Rosa canina leaflet EDGE, a curved oval blade fragment with five sharp serrations, some smaller subsidiary teeth, cream lateral veins reaching teeth, no thorns or stinging hairs, blade portion only. BOTTOM LEFT: one COMPLETE imparipinnate Sambucus nigra leaf with exactly FIVE distinct separate leaflets on central rachis: one large terminal ovate-lanceolate acuminate leaflet plus two opposing pairs, all leaflets ovate-lanceolate with finely serrate edges, slightly asymmetric bases, green upper surface, long petiole below first pair, no continuous tissue between separate leaflets. BOTTOM RIGHT: enlarged fragment of matching Sambucus nigra leaflet margin, small sharp serrate teeth and cream veins; portion of blade only. p02: Create a NEW scientifically informed 2x2 botanical raster sprite sheet. Match Fronda reference style: bold dark brown contours, flat green/tan fills, pale cream simple veins; transparent alpha background, no text, no frames/arrows/shadows. Four fully isolated complete illustrations, ample gutters. TOP LEFT: one Foeniculum vulgare fennel leaf, a long central rachis branching twice to three times into many long VERY THIN threadlike green terminal segments, airy feathery ovate outline, like thin branching green threads not flat broad leaflets; short visible sheathing petiole base. NOT a fern with wide blades, not needle tufts along a woody pine twig. TOP RIGHT: one complete mature dry fennel fruit still attached to short pedicel, elongated oval-cylindrical tan/brown schizocarp about 3 times longer than wide, with five broad rounded pale longitudinal ribs on its visible exterior, two tiny divergent style remnants at top. No wings, hooks, berries or seed release; intact exterior view as in University of Trieste photo TSB19538. BOTTOM LEFT: one complete Conium maculatum poison hemlock leaf, overall triangular outline, long petiole and central rachis, blade divided three times into smaller ovate-lanceolate segments; ultimate green blade segments are WIDE enough to show small lobes and pointed teeth, not hairlike threads. Branching fern/parsley-like structure, each largest lateral division itself further pinnately divided. No flowers and no root. BOTTOM RIGHT: enlarged portion of a terminal Conium leaf segment edge: a green lobed blade portion with several acute small teeth and cream vein branching, isolated fragment not a whole leaf. Clearly contrast fennel filiform divisions with poison-hemlock broad cut segments. Reference facts Flora Helvetica2018 and University of Trieste real photos.

p03: NEW botanical educational 2x2 sprite sheet, four independent accurate organs on genuine transparent alpha. p04: Create a NEW 2x2 educational botanical raster sprite sheet, matching reference Fronda style: bold smooth dark-brown outlines, flat greens/cream fills, minimal shading, true transparent alpha background. Four wholly separate illustrations, ample 70px spacing, no text, frames, arrows or shadows. TOP LEFT: Conium maculatum flowering COMPOUND UMBEL seen obliquely: eight to ten slender green unequal main rays all arise from one point, each ends in a small secondary umbellet of tiny white five-petalled flowers. Three short green reflexed bracts visible below main junction, not a leafy collar. Clear two-tier architecture, not a flat daisy head or branching corymb. TOP RIGHT: close exterior view of ONE Conium maculatum IMMATURE FRUIT, small ovate green schizocarp with a central seam and pale longitudinal ribs whose ridges are WAVY/scalloped rather than straight, minute style remnants at apex, on a very short slender pedicel, no spines or wings. The fruit must be short ovate, not fennel's long cylindrical fruit. BOTTOM LEFT: ONE complete Achillea ligustica leaf, overall ovate triangular outline, central narrow rachis with several lateral divisions; each division further cut into broad ovate-lanceolate lobed segments, lightly toothed terminal lobes; green blade with visible cream main vein. A finely divided but BROAD-SEGMENTED leaf, not filiform fennel and not dense narrow Achillea millefolium feather. Reference University of Trieste TSB53900. BOTTOM RIGHT: ONE Achillea ligustica flower HEAD (capitulum), enlarged oblique front view: five short broad WHITE ligules around a compact central disk of small cream/yellowish tubular florets, with several narrow green involucral bracts beneath, all together one small composite head on short stalk. No large daisy with 20 rays, no giant single flower, no branching umbel. No invented red/black spots. Morphology checked to Flora Helvetica (Conium) and University of Trieste photos for Achillea ligustica.
